acceptance_predicates.description: Every public command error, operation failure, partial outcome, and warning producer on the implementation baseline is mapped to the diagnostic catalog.

Known causes remain distinct through the public boundary; missing parent, absent input, conflict, type, permission, read-only, topology, malformed input, stale identity, capability, provider, transport, timeout, cancellation, reconciliation, and product failures do not collapse into generic buckets.

Diagnostics carry the affected resource role, safe target context, operation phase, state-change result, and validated remediation needed for useful human output without secrets or private internal data.
Error, failure, warning, and partial-success meanings are explicit and independently preserve existing exit-code and mutation semantics.
Adding a public diagnostic source or cause requires an explicit catalog mapping; no generic free-form public fallback silently accepts it.

definition_of_done: The reviewed inventory covers CLI, easy, routed TUI, setup/config/auth, project/tool/catalog, plan/run/sweep, report/compare, record/replay, provider/network, filesystem, and warning paths.
Fine-grained typed diagnostic and privacy tests pass without changing explicit JSON schemas or exit meanings.
Independent review and exact-head hosted checks pass.

inputs.description: AR-1757 command-aware human presentation and exhaustive public command inventory.
Merged project, tool installation/discovery, setup, execution, and lifecycle commands at the exact implementation baseline.

outputs.description: Closed fine-grained diagnostic identities, severity, safe context, state-change semantics, and remediation metadata.
Reviewed mapping from every public diagnostic producer to its catalog entry.

gates.description: All public diagnostic producers and every typed cause map exhaustively to the closed catalog.
Focused tests prove known lower-level causes retain their finest useful distinction through the CLI boundary.
Safe context is human-useful while machine schemas, exits, streams, and secret/private-data boundaries remain compatible.
